chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah, from his father (peace be upon him), said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A servant does not withhold Zakat, so it increases in his wealth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of paying Zakat on a person's wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi through the chain of Al-Sakuni, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys the Prophet’s (SAWW) promise that withholding Zakat acts as a spiritual and economic deterrent, causing wealth to stagnate or diminish. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the concept of 'Barakah' (divine blessing), where timely payment purifies assets and invites growth, while delay invites 'Qabd' (constriction).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘A servant would not withhold Zakāt, so there would be an increase in his wealth’.
en.sarwar: 20. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from af-Nawfafiy from al-Sakuniy from abu ’Abd Allah from his father, ‘Alayhim al- Salam, who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘If a person withholds payment of zakat due on his wealth, his wealth does not increase.’”
